stance.label: US stocks hug the 200-day line, hike fears return; stay on plan

headline: Split US close: hawkish Fed minutes sink the Dow 1.1%; AMD lifts Nasdaq 0.4%
summary: US stocks have not bottomed; the selling just rotated. Fed minutes and Waller revived hike fears, health care and energy dragged the Dow, and AMD and Amazon held up the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 has closed 2 days below its 200-day line, just 0.3% under. Today, watch whether Taiwan holds 39,858; keep regular investing on plan.

watch.label: TAIEX bear line (−20% from high)
watch.note: 11/18 close 40,194.91, only 0.8% away; a break means bear-market territory

watch.label: S&P 500 200-day line
watch.note: 2 closes below so far, 0.3% under; 5 closes and a flat line would turn it weak

overview.lead: This was rotation, not a rebound: rate worries weighed on the Dow, chips and internet names held up the Nasdaq, and the S&P 500 still hugs its 200-day line.
points: The S&P 500 fell 0.23%, its 2nd close below the 200-day line.
The Dow fell 1.11% as health insurers sank on a new audit proposal.
The Nasdaq rose 0.42%, led by AMD (AMD) and Amazon (AMZN).
Nvidia (NVDA) fell 2.9% after earnings, a fifth straight loss, as succession worries outweighed results.
Gold ETF (GLD) fell 3.2% and energy fell 3.3%; safe havens and commodities retreated together.

focus.lead: None of the nine tracked names hit a new add tier today; QQQ tier 3 is still the closest, and Taiwan's two funds stopped falling in their 11/18 NAVs.
points: QQQ rose 0.4%, still 2.1% from tier 3.
SPY fell 0.3%, hugging its 200-day line, 4.0% from tier 2.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) NAV rose 1.7% on 11/18, back to −29.8% from its high.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV rose 1.2% on 11/18, −33.1% from its high, still the deepest of the nine.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV caught up with a 3.3% drop on 11/17 and does not yet reflect the 11/18 bounce.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) and AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) share 7 top-ten names, so Nvidia's slide weighs on both.

position.lead: No new add tier hit today; QQQ tier 3, 2.1% away, is still the closest.
points: QQQ tier 3 at 645.71, 2.1% away.
SPY tier 2 at 701.18, 4.0% away.
AB Select US Equity tier 2 at 85.08, 4.6% away (11/17 NAV).
AB International Technology tier 5 at 1,218.74, 6.6% away (11/17 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used every tier; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: The pressure is back on rates: the Fed minutes show nearly all officials expect more hikes, and December could bring more than 25 bp.
points: The October meeting held rates, with two members favoring a 25 bp hike.
Waller wants a hike in December and another in January.
The 2-year Treasury yield is 4.80%, with the short end rising on hike bets.
The 10-year yield is 5.07%, slightly lower at the long end; the curve is not inverted.
The high-yield spread is 3.43% (11/17), far from the 5% alarm line.

sentiment.lead: Sentiment is still in extreme fear, but this is not panic selling: VIX dipped and the volatility curve is only slightly inverted.
points: CNN Fear & Greed is 24.6, versus 35.9 a week ago.
VIX is 24.56, in the 93rd percentile of the past year.
Short-dated VIX sits slightly above 3-month VIX, a mild term-structure inversion.
The equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) is only −3.5% from its high; the decline is concentrated in mega-cap tech.
6 of 11 sectors are above their 200-day lines; breadth has not collapsed.

sectors.lead: Health care and energy were sold while consumer and internet names held up; semis stopped falling but did not bounce.
points: Health care fell 2.2%; UnitedHealth (UNH) and Humana (HUM) each fell about 6%.
Energy fell 3.3% as crude stocks jumped and WTI dropped 3.2%.
Consumer discretionary rose 1.8%; Target (TGT) beat estimates.
Software ETF (IGV) rose 1.3%, pausing the prior day's selling.
Semiconductor ETF (SMH) dipped 0.1%, still down 16% in a month.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan opens without a push from Wall Street: the SOX was flat, TSMC's ADR edged up, and three days of foreign selling still weigh.
points: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) rose 0.1%, still −34% from its high.
TSMC ADR (TSM) rose 0.8%, about a 9.9% premium to the local shares.
Foreign investors sold NT$76.6B on 11/18, about NT$156.7B over a week.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures stand at 99,438 contracts, not covered after settlement.
The NT dollar is at 32.96 (11/17); hike bets keep the US dollar firm, so outflow pressure remains.

watch.lead: Three things through Friday: Taiwan holding 39,858, Walmart earnings, and where AI money goes after Anthropic lists.
points: The TAIEX bear line is 39,858, only 0.8% away.
The TAIEX has closed 3 days below its 200-day line; 2 more with a flat line trigger the defense rule.
Walmart (WMT) reports before the US open on 11/19, a read on US consumers.
Anthropic priced at US$83 a share and lists on Nasdaq on 11/19 (US time).
US initial jobless claims come out on 11/19 (US time).

regime.lead: By the rules, US stocks are a pullback within an uptrend, leaning "pullback"; Taiwan is "pullback, but risk rising". Neither has turned bearish.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 has closed 2 days below its 200-day line, only 0.3% under, and the line is still rising.
The Nasdaq-100 is about 3.4% below its 200-day line, likewise just under a rising average.
Systemic lights: only 1 is on in the US (index below its 200-day line); credit, the economy and financial conditions show no stress.
The closest to turning on is the credit-spread light, but the high-yield spread at 3.43% is far from 5%.
Capitulation signals: 2 are on in the US (extreme fear, volatility term inversion); VIX is not at panic levels.
History: S&P 500 drops to this level are usually just corrections; only 19 of 197 episodes went past −20%.
Of the 92 that were similarly fast and still above the line, only 6 went past −20%.
What would flip the call: 5 S&P 500 closes below 7,347 with a flat line means weak.
3 systemic lights would mean a possible bear turn; Taiwan below 39,858 is a bear market by definition.

news.title: Split US close: Dow −561.25 pts (−1.11%) to 50,198.17; S&P 500 −0.23%; Nasdaq +0.42%
news.read: The S&P 500 has closed 2 days below its 200-day line, but losses centered on health care and energy; our regime call is still "pullback".

news.title: Fed October minutes: nearly all officials expect more hikes; some see room for more than 25 bp in December
news.read: Hike pressure is back and the 2-year yield rose; rates are the biggest outside risk in this correction, but the financial-conditions light is still off.

news.title: Waller: after a 25 bp hike in December, hike again in January; CME shows 69% odds of 50 bp by end-January
news.read: A former dove turning hawkish forces markets to price higher rates sooner; growth-stock valuations and the NT dollar both feel it.

news.title: Nvidia (NVDA) falls 2.89% to US$150.96, a fifth straight loss, as succession and China scrutiny outweigh results
news.read: Results and guidance cleared the bar yet the stock keeps falling, so markets are pricing governance risk; Nvidia is a top weight in QQQ and both AB funds.

news.title: AMD (AMD) rises 5.31% to US$530.14; Broadcom (AVGO) rises 3.65%
news.read: Money rotated within chips rather than leaving AI, so the SOX was flat: neutral for Taiwan's open.

news.title: US CMS proposes wider Medicare Advantage audits; UnitedHealth (UNH) and Humana (HUM) each fall about 6%
news.read: Health care drove the Dow's drop and has nothing to do with AI; the diversified AB Select US Equity takes some of the hit.

news.title: WTI crude falls 3.20% to US$83.26 as US crude stocks rise 3.38 million barrels; gold falls 3.17%
news.read: Cheaper oil eases inflation, but gold's slide shows safe-haven demand fading as hike bets build.

news.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at US$83 a share, above the US$70–78 range; lists as ANT on 11/19 (US time)
news.read: Pricing above range shows AI money is still around, but the new listing may also pull funds from existing AI heavyweights.
